summary:
Assam stands under India's national framework. No Assam-specific statute on legal gender recognition, criminal law or facilities was identified in the sources reviewed, so the national assessment applies to this state.

Complaint machinery under the national Transgender Persons Act has been reachable in Assam. Of the seven cases registered nationally under the Act in 2021, two were registered in Assam; the 2023 national tally recorded none in the state. A Queerbeat crime-data report of 30 January 2026 cautions that these national counts are themselves very small, 20 cases across 2019 to 2023, and attributes the low figures to police-registration bias, so the absence of Assam cases in the 2023 tally does not establish an absence of incidents in the state.

State welfare machinery was absent as of the most recent documentation held here. A December 2021 reply to parliament from the Press Information Bureau listed the twelve states and union territories that had constituted Transgender Welfare Boards under the 2019 Rules, and Assam was not among them. No later notification constituting a board for Assam appears in the sources reviewed.
tangentialFactors:
The 27.2% physical violence and 22.3% sexual violence figures cited in the Queerbeat report of 30 January 2026 come from a 2025 survey of transgender respondents and are national in scope, not Assam-specific. The report supplies no comparison figure for the general population, so the two percentages cannot be read as a measure of risk in Assam.

Assam's two registrations in 2021 and none in 2023 are raw counts drawn from national totals of seven and twenty respectively. They record where complaints were entered into the system, not where harm occurred, and the report's own caution about registration bias means the counts rank administrative practice rather than incidence.
localsOnly:
With no Transgender Welfare Board constituted in Assam as of December 2021, residents have no state welfare body of the kind the 2019 Rules provide for. Applications for welfare support must go through national schemes or the courts instead, and no later board is documented in the sources reviewed.

The Queerbeat finding that police registration is the limiting factor applies to residents directly: a complaint filed in Assam may never enter the national counts. The report presents its tally of 20 cases nationally across 2019 to 2023 as a floor rather than a measure of incidence, which means an unregistered complaint in this state leaves no trace in the official record.
outOfScopeNotes:
Whether Assam constituted a Transgender Welfare Board after December 2021 is unresolved. The sources reviewed carry no later reply to parliament, notification or state gazette entry on the point.

No Assam-specific court rulings, facilities rules or documented incidents of violence against trans people appear in the sources reviewed. The record for this state rests on two registration counts and one welfare-board list, which is a thin evidentiary base for judging day-to-day conditions.

Whether respondents from Assam were included in the 2025 survey behind the 27.2% and 22.3% figures is not stated in the sources reviewed.

The report's attribution of low official counts to police-registration bias is not broken out for Assam, so the scale of any under-registration in this state is unknown.
